title: The Clinical Value of Serum KL-6 Changes on Evaluating Disease Development in Different Diffuse Parenchymal Lung Disease
brief_summary: Diffuse Parenchymal Lung Disease(DPLD) is a chronic progressive fibrosis lung disease that with a highly variable clinical process.Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) is a high-molecular-weight glycoprotein, classified as human MUC1 mucin, that is produced mainly by regenerating type II pneumocytes.Serum levels of KL-6 have been shown to be elevated in patients with DPLD and could predict progress, but unaware of the differential threshold. The objective of this study was to perspectively and sequentially monitor serum KL-6 levels in patients with different DPLD,then analyze its clinical value and find the differential threshold.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinical diagnosis of PM/DM-ILD,RA-ILD,IPAF,IPF

Exclusion Criteria:

* Combined with pulmonary infection,pulmonary tuberculosis,carsinoma.
study_population: All subjects with a dignosis of DPLD refer to the American Thracic Society(ATS)/European Respiratory Society(ERS) or American College of Rheumatology statement.
